item.title: Morning Digest, Saturday 28 November 2026
item.description:
The Centre Party's council meets tomorrow with its leader's job reportedly on the line, a drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians, eurozone leaders pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to run the ECB, US trading partners push back on new tariffs, and OpenAI countersues Apple.

Everyone's talking about

Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian defence technicians

Two Rheinmetall Italia employees maintaining an air-defence radar site died on Thursday and a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani worker were injured. Kuwait and Italy blame Iran; Tehran denies it and calls the attack a false flag, while indirect US-Iran talks remain stalled.

Al Jazeera, 27 Nov

Eurozone leaders pick Hernández de Cos to lead the ECB

European Council President António Costa said on Thursday that eurozone states recommend the head of the Bank for International Settlements and former Bank of Spain governor to succeed Christine Lagarde in February; he would be the first Spaniard in the post. Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier were recommended for the executive board. After the European Parliament and the ECB give their opinions, leaders are expected to make the formal appointment at the December summit.

European Council, 26 Nov; Al Jazeera (AFP, Reuters), 26 Nov

Trading partners push back on Washington's new tariffs

China called the US finding of excess factory capacity a pretext and vowed to defend its interests; Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam and the EU also rejected it. The duties, likely from early 2027, would be 20 percent on China (possibly rising to 40), up to 15 percent on the EU and Japan and up to 35 percent on Vietnam; Washington and Beijing extended their trade truce by two months.

AP, 26 Nov; CNBC, 25 Nov

Wall Street has its best week since April 2025

The S&P 500 gained 5.6 percent over the holiday-shortened week. Anthropic, the first frontier AI lab to list, rose 11 percent on Friday to $91.88, above its $83 offer price but well below its first-day high of about $115.

AP, 27 Nov

World

Hamas weighs a response to Israeli strikes

Leader Khalil al-Hayya said the group cannot keep absorbing attacks and will discuss a response with other factions, after strikes killed at least ten people including Khaled Abu Nada of its political office. Israel now controls about two-thirds of Gaza, and at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire.

Reuters, 26 Nov

Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 cases

The Bundibugyo-strain outbreak, the country's worst, has crossed 12,000 confirmed cases, and some responders have been evacuated as fighting hampers the effort.

Reuters, NPR, 26 Nov

Sweden

Centre Party council decides tomorrow, and Thand Ringqvist may go if it says no

The 59-member förtroenderåd is expected to vote on Sunday on the leadership's plan to let Kristersson through in Monday's 13:00 vote and join an M-C-KD-L minority government. SVT's sources say Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist will resign if the council says no; she has majorities in the party board and Riksdag group behind her. Birgitta Ohlsson says she will vote against Kristersson regardless, and council member Aida Karimli will vote no; S, V and MP say their doors remain open if the council overrules her. If Kristersson loses, a fourth vote is due before Christmas, and a fourth failure means a snap election.

SVT, TV4, SVT Text, 26-27 Nov (resignation based on unnamed sources)

Vattenfall raises grid fees by 5 percent

About 900,000 households and businesses pay more from next year, which the company attributes to grid investment; Ellevio and Eon have not announced 2027 fees.

SVT Text (Ekot), 26 Nov

Iraq extradites two suspects wanted in Sweden

A 20-year-old suspected of recruiting for the Foxtrot network and a 21-year-old linked to a 2024 murder in Skärholmen are being sent back, which prosecutors credit to closer cooperation with Baghdad.

SVT Text (Åklagarmyndigheten), 27 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Sunday 29 November: Centre Party council decides on the Kristersson government; snap general election in Spain.
  • Monday 30 November: Riksdag votes on Kristersson as prime minister at 13:00; appeal verdict in Sarkozy's Libyan campaign-financing case; AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.
  • Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires; Estonia closes its land border with Russia.
  • Thursday 3 December: Jensen Huang testifies to the US Senate Banking Committee.

SVT; Riksdagen; earlier editions

Tech and AI

OpenAI countersues Apple

OpenAI filed its own suit on Friday, escalating the trade-secrets fight that Apple started in July when it accused former employees of taking confidential hardware information to OpenAI.

CNN, 27 Nov; Apple's original suit: Al Jazeera, 10 Jul

Nvidia pauses server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries

It told partners including Dell and Super Micro to halt deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks compliance with a new US rule closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent Nvidia chips in data centres abroad, a source the Institute for Progress puts at about a quarter of China's AI compute.

TechCrunch (citing WSJ), FT via Reuters, 26 Nov

Chinese labs say the new rules will slow their next models

Zhipu's roughly 3-trillion-parameter GLM-5.5, planned for November, may slip to 2027, and Moonshot expects the gap between major releases to stretch from six months to a year or more if it loses overseas compute, pushing Kimi K4 towards mid-2027.

Reuters, 27 Nov (sources)

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Harness design for robot agents (Google with Emory, Ohio State and others): 470,000 simulated rollouts across eight benchmarks show that even frontier models fail when asked to output gripper poses directly, and work best when they hand motion to a trained action model through sub-goals and write checked control code; the combined recipe lifts frozen action models by up to 43 points without retraining (arXiv 2611.34778, alphaXiv).
  • Drawing doesn't help models think yet (Princeton, Meta): having a vision-language model request a generated helper image before answering lowered accuracy in 106 of 130 pipeline-task pairs, by 3.7 points on average and 21 on small-object search, mostly because the model asked for the wrong picture (arXiv 2611.34935, alphaXiv).
  • OS-Omni (OS-Copilot team): a 300-task benchmark of long computer-use workflows across six operating systems finds the best agent, Claude Opus 5.5, at 68.5 percent against 77.3 for humans, with frontier models beating people on Linux but trailing by over 25 points on iOS and macOS (arXiv 2611.34232, second on Hugging Face daily papers).

arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 24-25 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Friday 27 November 2026
item.description:
The Centre Party leadership backs Kristersson ahead of Monday's vote, EU leaders leave Brussels without a budget deal, Trump says he asked Putin to pull back across Europe, and the Houthis hit a Saudi refinery.

Everyone's talking about

EU budget summit breaks up without a deal

Leaders spent about ten hours on Costa's compromise for 2028-34, which trims the Commission's roughly 2 trillion euro proposal by 204 billion, then cancelled Friday's session. Merz and the net payers want cuts of several hundred billion more, Macron called the cut a strategic error and left early, and Sweden, Denmark, Belgium and Austria reportedly walked out of sessions; leaders try again from 17 December.

EUobserver, 27 Nov; PiQ Markets, 26 Nov (walk-outs reported)

Trump says he told Putin to pull back across Europe

Writing on Thursday, Trump said he had asked Putin, at their meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC last week, to end military pressure on territories throughout Europe and called the Ukraine war a bloodbath. It follows Polish claims of a Russian airspace violation and Estonia linking an arson attack to Russian military intelligence.

Reuters via Korea Times, 27 Nov

Houthi strike reaches a Saudi Aramco refinery

An attack on Aramco's Jazan refinery killed one worker, injured several and halted some operations, days after the Houthis twice hit the sovereign wealth fund's tower in Riyadh and threatened Red Sea ports. Saudi officials did not name the attacker.

Saudi Energy Ministry via Al Jazeera, 26 Nov

Storm postpones the Macy's Thanksgiving parade for the first time

A nor'easter with gusts of up to 100 km/h pushed New York's parade to Saturday, the first postponement in its 100 years, as up to 80 million Americans travelled for the holiday.

Times of Israel liveblog (AP), 26 Nov

World

Israel threatens mass displacement in Gaza

The defence minister said a million Gazans could be forcibly moved if Hamas does not disarm; Israeli strikes killed at least nine people overnight despite the ceasefire, medics said.

Monitor the Situation brief, 26 Nov

Russian border guards to leave Armenia

Prime Minister Pashinyan says the Russian guards posted on Armenia's borders since 1992 will be fully withdrawn over the coming years, another step away from Moscow.

Meduza via Monitor the Situation, 26 Nov

Guinea-Bissau's junta delays elections by two years

The vote set for 6 December is pushed to November 2028, extending military rule.

ABC News, Al Jazeera, 26 Nov

Five NATO countries order 430 combat vehicles

Described as the alliance's largest joint vehicle purchase; Finland says the supplier is BAE Systems.

Reuters via Monitor the Situation, 26 Nov

Sweden

Centre Party leadership says yes to Kristersson

After a several-hour meeting on Thursday, a majority of the Centre Party board and Riksdag group backed voting for Ulf Kristersson on Monday and joining a four-party M-C-KD-L minority government. Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist said C has no deal with the Sweden Democrats: no budget cooperation, no SD ministers, and C keeps a veto over policy. She said she would have resigned had the choice been a government with the Left Party or a snap election. The party's council (förtroenderåd) must still approve, reportedly on Sunday.

SVT, TT via Dagens PS, TV4, 26 Nov

Dissent inside C, welcome from the right

C's women's federation, youth wing and MEPs oppose a government that could rest on SD, and MP Anna Lasses says she will vote no. Kristersson, Busch and Mohamsson welcomed the decision; Magdalena Andersson predicts a historically weak government.

TV4, SVT, 26 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Sunday 29 November: Centre Party council decides on the Kristersson government; snap general election in Spain.
  • Monday 30 November: Riksdag votes on Kristersson as prime minister at 13:00; appeal verdict in Sarkozy's Libyan campaign-financing case; AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.
  • Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires; Estonia closes its land border with Russia.
  • Thursday 3 December: Jensen Huang testifies to the US Senate Banking Committee.

Riksdagen; SVT; TV4; earlier editions

Tech and AI

OpenAI puts ChatGPT and Codex on one meter

From December, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers draw on a single token-based allowance across chat and coding work, with quick 'Instant' chats left outside it; OpenAI says only a small share of heavy users will hit limits sooner.

TechCrunch, The Verge via The Neuron and DEV, 26 Nov

Cognition builds its new coding model on Kimi K3

SWE-2.1, the model behind Devin, was trained with reinforcement learning on top of Moonshot's open-weight 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3, a sign that Chinese open bases now anchor US products; Cognition reports roughly doubled scores on agentic coding tests but still ranks it behind the top closed models.

Cognition via DEV digest, 24-26 Nov

Ant Group releases Ling-3.2-air with open weights

The multimodal model, aimed at office automation through software tools, is downloadable under the MIT licence; on Ant's own test it completes 61 percent of tasks, against 16 percent for its predecessor.

The Neuron, 26 Nov (reported)

Brussels proposes a 50 billion euro tech equity fund

Henna Virkkunen presented a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund for AI and quantum, meant to draw up to six private euros per public euro, alongside a draft Quantum Act favouring EU-controlled firms in public procurement. Member states and Parliament must still agree.

DEV digest, 26 Nov (reported)

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (HUST, ByteDance Seed): a looped model that passes keys and values rather than the residual stream between loops, so decoding needs only one pass; at 700M parameters it matches OLMo3's final loss with 1.7 times fewer tokens, at twice the training compute (arXiv 2611.34923, high on Hugging Face and alphaXiv).
  • Stable Gated DeltaNet-2 (MemTensor, Jianlin Su and others): traces long-context training blow-ups in the new GDN-2 linear attention to a lopsided erase step that lets state values grow past 10^36 under a normal-looking loss, and fixes it with symmetric erasure, adding 6.8 points on 128K-token RULER (arXiv 2611.34051).
  • RL can be recovered from its own rollouts (CMU and others): simply fine-tuning a base model on the archived samples of an RL run, correct and incorrect alike, one step per batch, reproduces the whole learning curve without rewards, suggesting most RL compute goes into finding a better sampling distribution (arXiv 2611.33102, trending on alphaXiv).

arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 25 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Thursday 26 November 2026
item.description:
AI labs post a burst of claimed breakthroughs in core algorithms, Washington readies new tariffs on China and the EU, a US jury convicts Huawei, the Centre Party leader is reported to see only Kristersson or a snap election, and EU leaders meet on the budget and Ukraine.

Everyone's talking about

AI systems claim results at the heart of computer science

Google Research's multi-agent system Cogentic, running on Gemini models, posted six papers on Wednesday, among them an unconditional integer-factoring algorithm and faster discrete logarithms in some finite fields; OpenAI's repository added claims of a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming (Smale's ninth problem) and a disproof of the polynomial Hirsch conjecture on polytope diameters. None is peer reviewed yet: Google says its earlier results were checked by human experts, and OpenAI withdrew three of its own preprints in October. Commenters note the factoring result does not threaten RSA in practice. Scott Aaronson called the pace a turning point in his field.

Google Research GitHub via deniz.in and daily.dev; Snape Report; Shtetl-Optimized; 24-25 Nov (claims unverified)

US prepares new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others

After an inquiry into foreign overcapacity, trade representative Jamieson Greer is readying duties of up to 20 percent on China and 15 percent or less on the EU, Japan and South Korea, rebuilding the tariff regime the Supreme Court struck down in February. Legal challenges are expected.

WSJ and Politico via 10 Things Global News, 25 Nov (reported)

Huawei convicted on 10 of 12 counts in New York

A Brooklyn federal jury found the company guilty of bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets, over misleading banks about its Iran business; it was acquitted of racketeering and obstruction conspiracy. Huawei plans to appeal; sentencing is set for 14 September 2027.

Reuters, CNN, SCMP, 24-25 Nov

Houthis hit Saudi Arabia's sovereign fund headquarters again

A second strike in under a week on the Public Investment Fund's tower in Riyadh's financial district injured 11 people and led most international flights to Riyadh to be cancelled. The Houthis warned that Saudi Red Sea ports could be next; the Saudi-led coalition promised a firm response.

Al Jazeera, WSJ via 10 Things Global News, 25 Nov

Shanghai's party chief placed under investigation

Chen Jining is the fourth of the 24 Politburo members appointed in 2022 to be probed for discipline violations, leaving 19 active members, the fewest since 1999, a year before the next party congress.

Bloomberg, SCMP via 10 Things Global News, 25 Nov

World

EU leaders meet on the 2028-34 budget and Ukraine's 2027 money

The two-day special summit opening today weighs Costa's compromise budget and a 45 billion euro Ukraine package for 2027 (20 billion budget support, 25 billion military). Friedrich Merz has reportedly threatened to block the budget unless countries that stayed out of joint EU loans help pay the interest.

Interfax-Ukraine, 24 Nov; Kyiv Independent via Particle, 25 Nov

Venezuela discloses 237.5 billion dollars of public debt

The first official figures in years, published ahead of a sovereign restructuring, put debt at 242 percent of GDP, including 110 billion in defaulted bonds and interest; China and Russia hold about 22 billion.

FT, Bloomberg via 10 Things Global News, 25 Nov

Ebola responders trapped by fighting in eastern Congo

WHO staff are sheltering in a hospital maternity ward in Ituri as clashes continue; the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak that began in May has passed 11,600 confirmed cases and 5,600 deaths.

UN News, 24 Nov

China launches its first foreign astronaut to Tiangong

Shenzhou-24 lifted off on Wednesday carrying two Chinese crew and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign visitor expected on the Chinese station.

AP, DW via 10 Things Global News, 25 Nov

Sweden

Thand Ringqvist reportedly frames the choice as Kristersson or a snap election

At Tuesday evening's digital meeting with the party board and Riksdag group, the Centre Party leader is said to have argued that an Andersson-led government cannot take office because the Left Party will not drop its demand for cabinet seats, that abstaining to let the right through then sitting in opposition makes no sense when C is itself in the proposed government, and that C would be blamed for a snap election. No decision was taken. The Riksdag holds the first reading of Kristersson's nomination today, ahead of Monday's vote.

SVT, 24-25 Nov (based on unnamed sources)

Resistance inside C, and S rules out budget help

The Centre women's federation joined the youth wing in rejecting a Kristersson government, citing Sweden Democrat influence. Magdalena Andersson said S will not make budget deals with a four-party alliance government, and Justice Minister Gunnar Strömmer said such a government would need SD's tolerance, with support sought issue by issue.

TV4 via Metro Mode, 25 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Thursday 26 November: first reading of the prime-minister nomination in the Riksdag; special EU summit on the 2028-34 budget and Ukraine's 2027 funding opens, continuing Friday; US Thanksgiving, markets closed.
  • Friday 27 November: second reading of the nomination.
  • Sunday 29 November: snap general election in Spain.
  • Monday 30 November: Riksdag votes on Kristersson as prime minister at 13:00; appeal verdict in Sarkozy's Libyan campaign-financing case; AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.
  • Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires; Estonia closes its land border with Russia.
  • Thursday 3 December: Jensen Huang testifies to the US Senate Banking Committee.

Riksdagen; SVT; Interfax-Ukraine; Le Monde; earlier editions

Tech and AI

1Password breached through an employee's GitHub account

An attacker used the account to copy source code, push code into internal systems and take customer names, emails and account metadata for a subset of users; the company says vaults and the keys protecting them were never reachable and customers need only watch for phishing.

TechCrunch, 25 Nov; The Hacker News, 26 Nov

Tidal removes millions of fully AI-generated tracks

The streaming service says 43 percent of uploads over 90 days were made entirely by AI and will remove such tracks, millions in all, while still accepting music made with AI help.

The Guardian, TechCrunch, 24-25 Nov

New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years

Governor Kathy Hochul signed the ban, which takes effect in 90 days with fines of up to 15,000 dollars a day.

Office of the Governor of New York, 25 Nov

Amazon says an open-source agent exploited an unknown flaw on its own

Amazon reports catching an attack in which an open-source AI agent found and used a zero-day vulnerability with little human direction.

Gizmodo, 25 Nov (reported)

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Loom attention (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, ColorfulClouds): lets each attention head choose, token by token, which earlier heads to read from via a small per-token matrix memory; for 2-3 percent extra compute a 2.8B model trained on 300B tokens matches Pythia-12B on ten benchmarks (arXiv 2611.30634, high on Hugging Face).
  • RL with Verifiable Beliefs (Nanyang Technological University): agents that guess before they have enough evidence are trained with a reward computed from the simulator's exact posterior, so a lucky guess earns nothing; accuracy rises 17 percent on average across three benchmarks, where plain outcome-reward GRPO and PPO fall below the untrained model (arXiv 2611.32884).
  • Recursive Collective Intelligence (Stanford, Berkeley, NVIDIA): judges agent teams against compute-matched voting rather than a single agent, finds that only passing information between agents beats it, and shows label-free training on a group's own outputs improving it for four to six generations (arXiv 2611.32606, top of alphaXiv).

arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 24-25 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Wednesday 25 November 2026
item.description:
The Speaker has nominated Ulf Kristersson for a Monday vote without knowing how the Centre Party will vote, Washington is again discussing strikes on Iran's leadership, Estonia and Russia trade warnings over a closed border, and OpenAI claims to have pinned down the exact speed limit of matrix multiplication.

Everyone's talking about

Washington reopens the question of striking Iran's leaders

NBC News reported on Tuesday that the Trump administration is again weighing attacks on senior Iranian figures to force an end to a war now in its ninth month, with no decision taken and some military officers warning of retaliation. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said the same day that Tehran will not negotiate until seven conditions are met, among them lifting sanctions and ending the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

NBC News via GSM Global; 10 Things Global News, 24 Nov (reported)

OpenAI claims the exact speed limit of matrix multiplication

A preprint posted on Tuesday argues that the matrix-multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4, over every field: it both matches October's algorithm at about n to the 2.25 and proves no arithmetic circuit can do better. The best known upper bound had been about 2.371 and the best lower bound only the trivial 2. The work is AI-assisted, unreviewed, and only partly formalised in Lean, and changes nothing about how GPUs multiply matrices today.

OpenAI math preprint, 24 Nov; AI Weekly, OfficeChai, 25 Nov (claim not yet verified)

Estonia closes its Russian border, Moscow warns of 'open war'

Russia's foreign ministry accused Estonia on Monday of acts that risk open war after Tallinn decided to shut its land crossings from 1 December for at least six months, citing an alleged Russian-linked arson attempt on a defence firm. NATO's Mark Rutte said the alliance is watching, a week after a Russian missile crossed into Polish airspace.

10 Things Global News, 24 Nov

Leaked Russian statistics point to far higher war deaths

Researchers working from leaked Rosstat records put Russian military deaths at at least 490,000 by September, with higher estimates above 700,000, and document 1,087 military suicides since the full-scale invasion. Carnegie's Michael Kofman still expects Russia to recruit about 409,000 soldiers this year.

10 Things Global News, 24 Nov (reported)

World

Burnham rules out an EU referendum this parliament

The British prime minister told Parliament on Monday that rejoining the EU without a referendum would be unthinkable, and that the single market and customs union stay off the table for this parliament. He will set out options for closer ties next month; last week's deals on food checks, emissions trading and youth mobility are estimated to be worth about 17 billion pounds a year eventually.

10 Things Global News, 24 Nov

Solomon Islands drops its security pact with China

Honiara has reportedly told Beijing it will not renew the 2022 security agreement when it expires in April, and is due to sign a broader treaty with Australia in Canberra today, with Australian funding reported at 980 million dollars through 2028.

10 Things Global News, 24 Nov (reported)

Sweden

Kristersson nominated for a Monday vote, with the Centre Party still undecided

After receiving Kristersson's final sounding report on Tuesday afternoon, Speaker Andreas Norlén nominated him as prime minister for a government of M, C, KD and L, with readings in the chamber on Thursday and Friday and the vote on Monday 30 November at 13:00. Norlén said plainly that Kristersson does not yet know where the Centre Party stands, and called the risk of a snap election tangible: this is the third of four possible attempts, and a fourth failure forces an extra election within three months.

Riksdagen, SVT, TV4, 24 Nov

The Centre Party's red line against SD is the open question

Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist said she is ready to talk to both sides but would not say whether cooperation with the Sweden Democrats is ruled out, prompting a written clarification that the party's line has not changed; deputy leader Ulrika Heie called SD cooperation irrelevant. She briefed the party board, parliamentary group and local representatives at a digital meeting on Tuesday evening, after 35 Centre politicians publicly opposed governing with SD support. Jimmie Åkesson has said SD would stand aside and let a four-party government through without ministerial posts, but promises no support for its policies.

SVT, Sejfer, TV4, 24 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Wednesday 25 November: EU-Western Balkans summit in Brussels; Solomon Islands and Australia expected to sign their treaty in Canberra.
  • Thursday 26 November: first reading of the prime-minister nomination in the Riksdag; special EU summit on the 2028-34 budget and Ukraine's 2027 funding, continuing Friday; US Thanksgiving, markets closed.
  • Friday 27 November: second reading of the nomination.
  • Sunday 29 November: snap general election in Spain.
  • Monday 30 November: Riksdag votes on Kristersson as prime minister at 13:00; AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.
  • Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires; Estonia's border closures with Russia take effect.
  • Thursday 3 December: Jensen Huang testifies to the US Senate Banking Committee.

Riksdagen; SVT; Reuters; 10 Things Global News; earlier editions

Tech and AI

OpenAI says GPT-6 models design proteins that work in the lab

In tests with the lab Onava, GPT-6.2 reasoned and wrote code to design binders for five human protein targets, of which 35 of 322 bound, and redesigned antibody loops that still bound in 128 of 182 variants. Specialised tools still generated and filtered sequences, and OpenAI cautions that binding is not specificity or stability.

OpenAI via Unite.ai and Techlantis, 24-25 Nov

DeepMind agents cut quantum algorithm costs with machine-checked proofs

Teams of Gemini 4 agents working inside the Lean theorem prover found circuits with proven correctness and cost, reducing a fixed-point arcsin routine 290-fold and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug metabolism by 11.8, 8.2 and 2.5 times. Formal proof is what allows designs on thousands of qubits that no classical computer can test.

Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI, arXiv 2611.09822, 17-24 Nov

US blacklists a Singapore AI infrastructure firm

Megaspeed was added to the trade blacklist over alleged exports of Nvidia chips to China; the company denies wrongdoing. Enforcement of the chip controls now reaches third-country cloud providers.

BBC via The Neuron, 24 Nov

On the radar

Research pulse

  • RoboThink (Tulane, NYU, Stanford, MIT, Harvard and others): instead of letting a reasoning model drive a robot directly, it teaches the robot's action module to read short corrective feedback such as 'push right, slightly'; on LIBERO with an unknown constant drift on its motion commands, success rises from 0.09 to 0.87, at 55 seconds and 8,000 tokens per success against 2.1 minutes and over a million tokens for the model acting alone (arXiv 2611.30111).
  • WorldLeague (National University of Singapore): 60 simulated robot tasks scored on physical goals rather than answers; the best of 13 systems reaches 28.58 out of 100 and completes 13 tasks, and in 249 of the 347 episodes where a model answered every question about the scene correctly it earned zero credit for what it actually did (arXiv 2611.30989, high on both Hugging Face and alphaXiv).
  • RoboUniverse-10K (Tsinghua, Einsia.AI, Peking University and others): 10,807 resettable physics environments rebuilt automatically from real-world video, with 500 held out as a benchmark; frontier models reach 85.8 percent success against 2.6-10 percent for open models, and fine-tuning a 35B open model on 17,000 agent trajectories lifts it from 0.8 to 21.2 percent (arXiv 2611.31002).

arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 23-24 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Tuesday 24 November 2026
item.description:
The Centre Party reopens talks with Kristersson's side on the morning the Speaker meets the party leaders, Nvidia's board takes Jensen Huang back after US government input, Anthropic posts a Claude-written proof of the algebraic version of P versus NP that no human has yet checked, and Z.ai launches a looped 750-billion-parameter model.

Everyone's talking about

Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive

Eleven days after he resigned and six days after the board said it would not take him back, Nvidia's directors voted unanimously on Monday to restore Huang as CEO with immediate effect. The company says it acted after 'input from senior levels of the United States government' that his return poses no national-security risk; an inquiry into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort continues, and interim CEO Colette Kress returns to her finance role.

Nvidia press release (SEC filing); SCMP, 17-23 Nov

Anthropic posts a Claude-written proof that VP differs from VNP

A 70-page paper credited solely to Claude, with a Lean formalisation reported at about 73,000 lines, claims to settle Valiant's 47-year-old conjecture, the algebraic counterpart of P versus NP, over every field, by proving that circuits computing the permanent need superpolynomially many gates. Anthropic's own notes say no human mathematician has yet checked it and that nothing verifies that the Lean statement matches the claim; it does not settle P versus NP itself.

Interesting Engineering; CASRAI, 23-24 Nov (claim not yet verified)

Ukraine says it hit a Russian warship in Libya

Zelenskyy confirmed on Monday that Ukraine was behind Sunday's strike on a Russian corvette at a naval base in eastern Libya, its farthest attack on Russia's navy so far; the Kremlin called it terrorism.

Reuters world summary via Devdiscourse; AP via Just Security, 22-23 Nov

World

Report: NATO expects a Russian nuclear-armed satellite launch

German media say NATO intelligence has concluded that Russia will put a satellite carrying a nuclear weapon into orbit this year, which would breach the 1967 Outer Space Treaty.

Reuters via Devdiscourse and Just Security, 23 Nov (reported)

Eisenkot calls settler attacks 'Jewish terrorism'

Israel's prime minister-designate used the term after arson attacks on West Bank villages, an unusually blunt line for an incoming Israeli leader.

Reuters via Just Security, 22 Nov

Sweden

Centre Party reopens talks with M, KD and L

After an extra meeting on Monday evening, Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist said the party will resume talks with the Moderates, Christian Democrats and Liberals so the process does not stall, noting that the Left Party had still not given a clear answer to Sunday's final offer from S, C and MP. It is not yet a decision to back Kristersson, but it is the first open move by C towards the right since it chose Andersson's side on 15 November. Left deputy leader Ida Gabrielsson responded that she regrets C's 'switch of sides'. Kristersson reports to the Speaker this morning.

TT via Hallands Nyheter, 24 Nov; SVT, 18 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Tuesday 24 November: the Speaker meets the party leaders from 09:30, Kristersson at 10:00 with his report; press conference no earlier than 16:30.
  • Wednesday 25 November: EU-Western Balkans summit in Brussels.
  • Thursday 26 to Friday 27 November: special EU summit on the 2028-34 budget and Ukraine's 2027 funding; Thursday is US Thanksgiving, markets closed.
  • Sunday 29 November: snap general election in Spain.
  • Monday 30 November: AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.
  • Late November: a possible third prime-minister vote in the Riksdag, date not yet set.
  • Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires.

SVT; Riksdagen; Reuters; Everything Briefing; earlier editions

Tech and AI

Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, a looped transformer

The Chinese lab's new flagship runs 28 layers of its GLM-5 model twice, gaining depth without adding parameters; at about 750 billion parameters, Z.ai says it matches models of 2-3 trillion. It is live for coding-plan subscribers, with the API and open weights promised after safety testing and no benchmarks published yet.

Z.ai via TestingCatalog and CellCog, 23 Nov

SpaceX plans $74 billion of AI campuses

The company's planned AI facilities in Texas and Arizona would draw about 6 gigawatts in Arizona alone at full build-out, roughly the output of six large nuclear reactors, raising questions about who pays for grid upgrades.

Fortune via The Neuron, 22-23 Nov (reported)

Meta reconsiders its 2030 net-zero goal

Its reported emissions rose about 40 percent in a year, to more than 21.7 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2025.

Ars Technica via The Neuron, 23 Nov

Startup says AI agents designed a more efficient CPU

Architect Labs claims its 'Frostbite' design delivers 4.59 times the performance per watt of a comparable simple processor in 7-nanometre simulation; no chip has been made and the comparison core is unnamed.

Tom's Hardware via The Neuron; explainx.ai, 19-23 Nov (company claim)

On the radar

Research pulse

  • cmHC (China Telecom's Xingchen AGI Lab and others): hyper-connections, which replace the single residual stream with several mixed streams, either barely mix or blur together; shrinking the allowed mixing matrices towards the interior of their polytope fixes both with no new parameters, tested on dense and mixture-of-experts pretraining (arXiv 2611.27193, top of Hugging Face daily papers).
  • NoPeWorld (PolyU): five of six interactive video world models let the player walk through walls, yet their hidden states already predict collisions; a small probe that vetoes unsafe moves cuts physical violations from 74 to 16 percent and ships with a new benchmark (arXiv 2611.27963, Hugging Face and alphaXiv hot lists).
  • MemOnce (Nanjing University, USTC): instead of storing keys and values for every layer, it keeps a small set of final-layer states and decodes them back on demand; adapting Qwen3.5-4B cut the memory cache 1,313-fold and prefill time 6.9-fold at a million tokens while scoring higher on memory tests (arXiv 2611.27973).

arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 20-23 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Monday 23 November 2026
item.description:
COP31 ends without its main deal, attacks on Gulf shipping reach their highest level of the war, drones set a Kaliningrad-bound ship alight in the Gulf of Finland, and the Left Party rejects Andersson's final offer within minutes, a day before the Speaker meets the party leaders.

Everyone's talking about

COP31 ends without an overarching deal

After nearly 48 hours of overtime in Antalya, the EU, Britain, Norway, Panama and the Marshall Islands blocked the Turkish-Australian 'Antalya Pact' on Sunday because it did not commit to moving away from fossil fuels, a line more than 130 countries had backed. Narrower decisions, including one on a just transition, were adopted; Guterres said he was disappointed.

Xinhua; Reuters via The Nation, 22-23 Nov

Attacks on Gulf shipping hit their highest level of the war

At least 25 tankers were struck in and around the Strait of Hormuz in seven days, and Iran says its latest strikes on US bases in Bahrain targeted radars after the US hit an Iranian radar on Hengam Island. War-risk insurance now costs 3.5-7.5 percent of a ship's value, up from 0.1-0.25 percent before the war; oil briefly passed $100 before settling near $83.

Al Jazeera, 22 Nov

Drones set a Kaliningrad-bound ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland

The cargo ship Sparta II was hit by two drones in international waters west of Gogland on Saturday, caught fire and drifted into Finnish waters, where it was still burning on Sunday. Finland reimposed air and sea restrictions in the eastern Gulf and Sweden offered help; no one has claimed the attack, Kyiv did not comment, and Prime Minister Orpo said Ukraine has the right to fight its aggressor.

Reuters via The Moscow Times; Bloomberg, 21-22 Nov

World

EU budget draft cut again, with a 3 percent digital tax

António Costa, who chairs EU summits, proposes a 2028-34 budget of €1,582 billion, €40 billion below the October compromise, cutting mainly the competitiveness fund, defence and external spending, and suggests a 3 percent levy on digital advertising and platform revenue that would fall mostly on US tech giants. Parliament's negotiator called it unacceptable; leaders discuss it Thursday and Friday.

Reuters via Yahoo Finance, 21 Nov

Trump weighs in as Schumer faces a leadership challenge

Trump wrote that it would be 'very hard' to work with Chuck Schumer as majority leader; Schumer, who leads Senate Democrats into a majority in January, faces Chris Van Hollen in a secret ballot on 1 December.

Reuters/AP via Al Jazeera, 22 Nov

Autonomous-weapons talks end without a ban

At the UN weapons convention in Geneva, 128 countries agreed only to 'elaborate' possible rules on lethal autonomous weapons by 2028; campaigners called the mandate watered down.

UN News and CNBC via AI Daily Digest, 21 Nov (reported)

Sweden

Left Party rejects Andersson's final offer in 20 minutes

On Sunday evening Magdalena Andersson, backed by the Centre and the Greens, offered the Left Party an eleven-point package: a seat in a four-leader inner cabinet, state secretaries and its own staff in the Prime Minister's Office and the budget unit, plus rent discounts and a dental reform, but no ministerial posts, its core demand. Ida Gabrielsson answered 'thanks, but no thanks' within 20 minutes. The Centre calls it the Left's last chance and wants a formal answer today; SVT's analyst sees a Kristersson-led government, or a snap election, as more likely.

SVT; TV4, 22 Nov

Wegovy tablet coming to Sweden

Novo Nordisk will soon sell its weight-loss drug as a daily pill in Sweden; the price is not set but is expected at a few thousand kronor a month.

Sweden Herald, 22 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Monday 23 November: the Left Party's formal answer to the S-C-MP offer is expected; Denmark presents its Russia visa curbs to EU ambassadors; UN special summit on AI safety in Bridgetown, Barbados.
  • Tuesday 24 November: the Speaker meets party leaders from 09:30 (Kristersson at 10:00 with his final report); press conference no earlier than 16:30.
  • Thursday 26 to Friday 27 November: special EU summit in Brussels on the 2028-34 budget and Ukraine's 2027 funding; Thursday is US Thanksgiving, markets closed.
  • Monday 30 November: Amazon's AWS re:Invent conference opens in Las Vegas.
  • Late November: a possible third prime-minister vote in the Riksdag, date not yet set.
  • Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats elect their leader, Schumer against Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires.

SVT; Riksdagen; Reuters; Kyiv Independent; earlier editions

Tech and AI

OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a yardstick and a limit

Jakub Pachocki published figures on OpenAI's pretraining progress, measured as loss on its internal test set (about 0.99 for GPT-3.5, 0.91 for GPT-4, around 0.76 for a model that has produced results on open maths problems), expects further jumps in the 0.68-0.7 range and possibly a burst of pretraining advances as soon as 2027. He proposes that labs agree on shared limits on such measures that none would cross until monitoring tools catch up; it is not a call for a pause.

OpenAI, 22 Nov

Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on data centres built abroad

He told a White House briefing that the US will not let its companies put data centres in other countries, framing it as part of the AI race with China, but gave no details and said he had not yet told his officials. US cloud giants have announced multi-billion-dollar data-centre investments abroad this year, including in Europe and Australia.

ABC News (Australia); CNBC, 20-21 Nov

Cognition reportedly raising at $75 billion

The maker of the Devin coding agent is in talks to raise more than $2 billion, its third round this year, according to Bloomberg; nothing is signed.

Bloomberg via AI Daily Digest, 20 Nov (reported)

On the radar

Research pulse

  • Clover-35B-A3B (DiffuSpace): an open-weight diffusion language model, converted from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, that writes blocks of tokens in parallel and remembers earlier text through a recurrent memory; it reports 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 680 tokens per second on one GB300, a step towards diffusion models competing on agentic coding (arXiv 2611.24636, top of Hugging Face daily papers).
  • Feedback Shortcut (Institute of Foundation Models, USC, CMU): models that feed each position's top-layer state back into the next position are stronger but break speculative decoding; a trained stand-in plus a correction folded into the next verification pass restores 2.4-2.8 times faster decoding at essentially full quality, tested at 135M and 780M parameters (arXiv, 20 Nov, alphaXiv hot list).
  • The content-geometry tradeoff (NYU and AMI Labs, with LeCun): JEPA world models trained with the usual stop-gradient learn jagged latent spaces that make poor maps for planning; a simple variance floor along random directions, plus a term favouring slowly changing features, gives the best planning in five control tasks and learns street maps from first-person city-walk video (alphaXiv hot list, Nov).

arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 18-22 Nov

item.title: Morning Digest, Sunday 22 November 2026
item.description:
The Lean and Mathlib communities certify the Claude-made proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, Iran strikes US bases in Bahrain as its tankers line up to run the blockade, COP31 nears a deal in Antalya, and a Centre Party MEP urges her party to give up on the red-greens and turn to Kristersson.

Today's must-read

GTIG AI Threat Tracker: Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold (Google Threat Intelligence Group)

Google's threat-intelligence team documents the first attack pipeline it has seen running with no human in the loop: a framework called exploit_agent that watches web software for security patches, compares the code before and after the fix, writes a working exploit for the flaw the patch reveals and launches it. The report also covers open-source AI hacking frameworks used in real intrusions, an influence-operations platform built to run more than 100,000 accounts, and a suspected North Korean group that planted a backdoor by editing Claude Code settings files. First-hand evidence of AI acting as the attacker, and why patched (rather than unknown) flaws become the main target once exploits can be written in hours.

Everyone's talking about

Lean community certifies the AI-made Riemann Hypothesis proof

In a joint statement on Saturday, the Lean and Mathlib communities, backed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative, said they have full confidence that Levent Alpöge's 17-million-line library is correct: it compiles, its final theorem matches Mathlib's own statement of the Riemann Hypothesis, and several independent checkers accept every step. What is still missing is a human-readable account of why the proof works. Separately, problems have reportedly been found in Alessandro Masullo's 940-page human-written draft released the same day.

Lean community blog; Shtetl-Optimized; Al Jazeera; AgentsPulse, 21-22 Nov

Iran strikes US bases in Bahrain as tankers prepare to run the blockade

On Saturday night Iran fired two waves of drones and ballistic missiles at four US bases in Bahrain, including the Fifth Fleet headquarters; Bahrain says it intercepted several and reports no injuries. Earlier, at least three tankers were hit near the Strait of Hormuz, and around 14 Iranian tankers are reported waiting off Kharg Island to break the US blockade, which Tehran calls an act of war.

Euronews; AP via ClickOrlando, 21 Nov

COP31 nears a deal after overtime

Summit president Murat Kurum announced consensus on a revised text in a late-night session in Antalya, with formal adoption scheduled for early Sunday; the earlier draft drew heavy criticism for leaving out any phase-out of fossil fuels, and the final wording is not yet public.

GMA News via Head Topics; AP, 21-22 Nov

World

Denmark asks the EU to stop tourist visas for Russians

After Danish intelligence tied a foiled plot against the Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner to Russia, Copenhagen expelled Russia's defence attaché and asked EU partners to suspend Russian tourist visas and stop accepting Russia's non-biometric passports; it presents the proposal to EU ambassadors on Monday. Moscow denies involvement.

Reuters via Kyiv Independent, 20-21 Nov

Eisenkot tasked with forming Israel's next government

Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot has received the mandate after October's election left no clear majority, which would make him the first leader since 2022 other than Netanyahu to attempt it.

CBS News live blog, 21 Nov (reported)

Sweden

Red-green talks locked as a Centre MEP urges a turn to Kristersson

The Left Party has turned down a Social Democratic offer of its own officials inside the Government Offices and still demands ministerial posts, and SVT's sources describe the mood after Friday's talks as resigned. On Saturday the Centre Party MEP Emma Ytterell wrote that the most responsible path is now a government with the other centre-right parties, saying the Left had several chances. TV4's sources in the Centre leadership say the party lacks support for such a switch and fear it would split the party. The Social Democrats' published programme includes scrapping the unpaid first sick day, banning profit-making in schools and raising the age of criminal responsibility to 15. All party leaders meet the Speaker on Tuesday.

SVT; TV4; TT via SVT Text, 20-21 Nov

Police to open a station in Iraq

National police chief Petra Lundh told Ekot that a pilot station will open in Iraq early next year to reach gang leaders who direct violence in Sweden from abroad; four more foreign stations are planned over four years.

SR Ekot via SVT Text, 21 Nov

Unemployment falls to 8.6 percent

Statistics Sweden says seasonally adjusted unemployment fell in October while employment rose.

SCB via SVT Text, 20 Nov

Week ahead

Scheduled

  • Monday 23 November: UN and Barbados host a Special Summit on AI Safety in Bridgetown; Denmark presents its Russia travel curbs to EU ambassadors, and the Commission's 22nd sanctions package is reportedly due.
  • Tuesday 24 November: the Speaker meets party leaders from 09:30 (Kristersson at 10:00 with his final report); press conference no earlier than 16:30.
  • Thursday 26 to Friday 27 November: EU leaders' summit in Brussels on Ukraine's 2027 funding and the 2028-34 budget; Thursday is US Thanksgiving, markets closed.
  • End of November: a possible third prime-minister vote in the Riksdag, date not yet set.
  • During the week: Sweden, Germany and the Netherlands expected to sign the Pax Silica declaration on AI supply chains.

UN; Kyiv Independent; SVT; Riksdagen; earlier editions

Week in review

AI moved from helping mathematicians to settling famous problems

On Tuesday Anthropic said Claude had solved two open problems in black-hole physics; on Friday an Anthropic mathematician released a Claude-made proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and, with an NYU colleague, a claimed Navier-Stokes blow-up, and by Saturday the Lean community had certified the first. The common thread is again the proof checker: it is what lets anyone trust results that no human has yet fully read.

The AI trade cracked in the week of its biggest listing

SemiAnalysis cut its forecasts for AI chip spending by up to 41 percent for later years, Anthropic priced the largest listing ever at $83 a share and rose 17 percent on its first day, and then reports of an SEC look at Nvidia's accounting gave the chipmaker its worst week in 18 years and pushed the S&P 500 into a correction. Anthropic ended the week close to its listing price.

Summits and signatures, but the wars widened

Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen and signed a four-point declaration that left out every war. Meanwhile US-Iran fighting spread to Kuwait and Bahrain, Russia launched one of its largest air attacks on Ukraine, and the Senate declined to limit Trump's war powers. The one deal that did close was Britain's reset with the EU.

Tech and AI

Anthropic's compute spending grows faster than OpenAI's

Epoch AI estimates Anthropic's spending on compute is rising about fourfold a year against roughly threefold at OpenAI, and that capacity for agentic inference, meaning models running long multi-step tasks, grew 4.6 times in a year while total compute capacity grew 2.6 times.

Epoch AI, 18 Nov

Walmart says shoppers using its AI agent buy 40 percent more

Use of its Sparky assistant more than doubled in the US, and the company is building a gateway to control how outside AI shopping agents reach its store, an early sign of retailers setting rules for agent-driven buying.

Walmart Q3 results via RIO Rundown, 20-21 Nov

Runway's revenue doubles to $200 million a year

The AI video company reached that annualised revenue in September and is extending its Praxis-1 world models, which simulate how scenes evolve, to robotics.

Bloomberg via RIO Rundown, 21 Nov (reported)

On the radar

Research pulse

  • A Society of AI Scientists (alphaXiv, MIT, Stanford and others): over twelve weeks 936 autonomous agents across 35 labs published 936 studies, critiqued each other in 229 chat rooms and even founded their own peer-review journal; blind reviewers rated the agents' work more rigorous but less novel than recent human preprints (arXiv, 21 Nov, alphaXiv hot list).
  • Harnesses as compositional generalisers (MIT CSAIL, Zhang and Khattab): training a Recursive Language Model harness with RL on short tasks generalises to tasks 2-64 times longer, because each model call stays on familiar ground; their RLM-27B, trained only on synthetic surrogate tasks, scores 26.9 percent higher on hard long-context benchmarks with about half the tokens (arXiv, Nov, alphaXiv hot list).
  • TideCache (MIT, ETH Zurich, UCSD): a serving system for hybrid models that mix full attention with cheaper recurrent layers, streaming each attention layer's cache from CPU memory just in time on Nvidia's GB300 and GH200 superchips; it completes up to twice as many agent turns and cuts per-token latency by 20-59 percent (arXiv 2611.26619).

arXiv via alphaXiv, 19-21 Nov
